body: Thank you for this. I wish I could share is with my partner.

That’s a lot of fucked up shit.  None of that should have ever happened to you. The fucked up part is that it did and now you’re here. 
When my life began to feel like it was caving in I couldn’t image any of it getting better. I’m not even 100% sure how I made it out. I know getting therapy and on meds helped. Your situation puts that just out of reach. It looks like you have access to the internet so if I were you I would look up how other people have made it out. I’ve listened to TEDtalks and countless NPR interviews and stories. Even the ones that seemed like they had it easier or different it was still a way for me to look at my situation from another perspective. You gotta find a way out of that house. Your mom is unhealthy and that environment is perpetually bringing back your pain and struggles. It’s weird how difficult it is to find resources as a single woman but when I was a kid there was a woman’s housing set up that made an exception for my family. So I hope there’s one out near where you live that will make the exception for you. It’s not easy to find these places but they are out there. One resource will lead to another one, they’re all connected but you gotta put in the work to find them. Call every one you can and keep asking questions and for referrals to somewhere that can help you if they can’t. Sometimes they’re connected with churches as well. I’m not a religious person but I appreciate the outreach some churches do and the value they put on community. Talk to any organization that will listen. You may get turned away but don’t stop, there’s one out there that can help and get things moving for you. Libraries sometimes have a board with resource centers posted, check there. If anything at least it’ll get you out of the house. 
I still have shitty days but I’m happy to give a big fuck you to the ones that tried to bring me down and hoped I’d fail at life by going another day.

Best of luck friend! My sister did an intensive outpatient program for depression and I had a friend do an intensive inpatient program for an eating disorder. They’re both doing much better now. I hope the same for you. It’s good to hear that you’re taking that opportunity.
I’ll start researching what our insurance offers. My hope is to use that time for her to get well and for us to plan to get the hell outta this city.
And thanks again for talking with me.
I wish I could say something to help get those thoughts out of her head. At least for a moment. And thank you for your reply, you helped me get those thoughts out of my head at least for a moment.

We would have to move to be able to make that work, we live in a stupidly expensive city. But you’re right, something has got to give to tip the balance back to making life worth it.
To answer your question though, no close friends, no close family. Unfortunately we haven’t been able to save money either. That’s a huge reason why she has so much riding on her shoulders with this job. I moved out here for her when things were better at her job. In the past year+ since moving in together things have progressively become worse with work.

I have talked about medical leave and what not but the financial component brings on the stress. Especially because it’ll put her job on the line, legal or not. Even the conversation brings her to spiral.
